title: The Wolf and the Lamb
text:
A wolf came to drink at a stream and saw a lamb drinking a little way below him. He wanted to eat it, but he also wanted a reason that would make the meal look just.

"Why are you muddying the water I drink?" he growled. The lamb answered gently that this was impossible: the stream flowed from the wolf down to her, so she could not foul his water. The wolf tried again. "Then it was you who insulted me six months ago." The lamb replied that six months ago she had not even been born.

The wolf was not bothered by being proved wrong twice. "If it was not you, it was your father," he said, and he sprang on the lamb and ate her.

The lamb had won every argument. It made no difference, because the wolf had decided what he would do before he opened his mouth, and the accusations were only there to dress up the decision.
lesson: When someone with power keeps changing the charge after each one is answered, the charges are not the real issue. Recognize a pretext early and stop expecting good arguments alone to protect you.
